source.method: git log -S / tag-range rev-list on a blobless torvalds/linux clone; semantics from drivers/block/ublk_drv.c

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_GET_QUEUE_AFFINITY
items.summary: Read the CPU set blk-mq maps to one hardware queue.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = queue id; `addr`/`len` = output buffer. `len` must be a multiple of
`sizeof(unsigned long)` and `len * 8 >= nr_cpu_ids` (`ublk_ctrl_get_queue_affinity`).

**Output:** a kernel cpumask (array of `unsigned long`, bit *n* = CPU *n*) of every possible CPU whose
`tag_set.map[HCTX_TYPE_DEFAULT].mq_map[cpu] == queue`; bytes past `cpumask_size()` are zeroed.

**Errors:** `EINVAL` (bad len, `addr == 0`, queue >= nr_hw_queues), `EFAULT`, `ENOMEM`, `ENODEV` (no such device).
Does not sleep, so since v6.19 (87213b0d847c) it is handled inline under `IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`). Permission mask for unprivileged devices: MAY_READ.

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_GET_QUEUE_AFFINITY` (0x01, since v6.0).
items.notes: Valid any time after ADD_DEV (the tag set exists from ADD_DEV). The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: Used by default to pin each queue's I/O threads to the CPUs the kernel routes to it (when DeviceParams.CPUAffinity is empty); ctrl.Controller.GetQueueAffinity.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO
items.details:
**Inputs:** `dev_id`; `addr`/`len` (len >= 64) receives the 64-byte `ublksrv_ctrl_dev_info`.

**Output:** the device's current info: negotiated flags, `state` (`UBLK_S_DEV_*`), queues, depth,
`max_io_buf_bytes`, `owner_uid/gid`, the opaque `ublksrv_flags`, and `ublksrv_pid` translated into the
caller's pid namespace (-1 if the server is gone or not visible; translation since v6.19-rc7, 47bdf1d29cae,
backported to 6.18.8).

**Errors:** `ENODEV` (no device with that id), `EINVAL` (len < 64, addr 0, or — for an unprivileged
device — no `dev_path_len`), `EFAULT`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO` (0x02, since v6.0).
items.notes: There is no list command: enumerate devices by probing ids or by reading `/sys/class/ublk-char/`. On an unprivileged device GET_DEV_INFO also needs the path prefix, which is how a client can tell the two apart. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_ADD_DEV
items.summary: Create a device (`/dev/ublkcN`) and negotiate queues, depth, buffer size and features.
items.details:
**Inputs:** header `queue_id` must be `0xffff`; header `dev_id` must equal `info.dev_id` (`U32_MAX` =
auto-assign, else < 2^20 since v6.7); `addr`/`len` (len >= 64) points at `ublksrv_ctrl_dev_info` with
`nr_hw_queues` (1..4096), `queue_depth` (1..4096), `max_io_buf_bytes`, `flags`, `ublksrv_flags`, and
`io_desc_size` (only with `UBLK_F_IO_DESC_SIZE`).

**Output (written back to `addr`):** assigned `dev_id`; `nr_hw_queues` clamped to `nr_cpu_ids`;
`max_io_buf_bytes` rounded down to `PAGE_SIZE`; `flags &= UBLK_F_ALL`, then forced on:
`CMD_IOCTL_ENCODE | URING_CMD_COMP_IN_TASK | PER_IO_DAEMON | BUF_REG_OFF_DAEMON | SAFE_STOP_DEV`
(PER_IO_DAEMON removed again with BATCH_IO; NEED_GET_DATA removed with USER_COPY / ZERO_COPY /
AUTO_BUF_REG / BATCH_IO; UNPRIVILEGED_DEV removed for a CAP_SYS_ADMIN caller; USER_RECOVERY and
REISSUE removed for an unprivileged device); `owner_uid/gid` = caller (init_user_ns ids);
`io_desc_size` = 24 unless IO_DESC_SIZE; `state` = DEAD and `ublksrv_pid` = -1 (reset since
e65848e4ce35, v7.2-rc6, backported to 6.1.183/6.6.151/6.12.103/6.18.44/7.1.8).

**Errors:** `EINVAL` (len/addr/queue_id, depth or queue count 0 or > 4096 [checked since v6.16,
8c8472855884, backported 6.6.95/6.12.35/6.15.4], dev_id mismatch or >= 2^20, bad recovery-flag
combination [v6.13+], QUIESCE without USER_RECOVERY, unprivileged with USER_COPY/ZERO_COPY/AUTO_BUF_REG,
INTEGRITY without USER_COPY, ZONED without USER_COPY/ZERO_COPY or without CONFIG_BLK_DEV_ZONED, bad
io_desc_size), `EPERM` (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN and no UNPRIVILEGED_DEV), `EACCES` (unprivileged device count
>= `ublks_max`), `EEXIST` (requested id in use), `EFAULT`, `ENOMEM`, `EINTR` (killable `ublk_ctl_mutex`).

Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, or `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` (v6.3+) by any user who can open
`/dev/ublk-control`. ADD_DEV never takes a path prefix.


Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_ADD_DEV` (0x04, since v6.0).
items.notes: Unknown flag bits are silently cleared, so the written-back `flags` is the negotiation result; compare it with what you asked for. Before v6.16 a zero or oversized depth/queue count was not rejected. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.AddDev` / `AddDevice`; public `ublk.Create`, `CreateAndServe`. Flags are pre-validated against the 7.3-rc5 rules (`ctrl.ValidateFeatures`, `ctrl.Negotiate`).

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_DEL_DEV
items.summary: Remove a device and wait until its id is free.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `dev_id`; no buffer.

**Behaviour:** `ublk_ctrl_del_dev(wait=true)`: stops the device if it is still started
(`ublk_stop_dev`), deletes `/dev/ublkcN`, drops the creation reference, then waits interruptibly until
the device number is released — i.e. until the last reference (open `/dev/ublkcN`, its mmaps, the
release work) is gone. Calling it from a process that still holds `/dev/ublkcN` open blocks until that
process closes it or a signal arrives.

**Errors:** `ENODEV`, `EINTR` (interrupted wait; the device is still deleted, v6.5+ 3e9dce80dbf9),
`EINTR`/killed on the `ublk_ctl_mutex`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_DEL_DEV` (0x05, since v6.0).
items.notes: Close and munmap everything on `/dev/ublkcN` before DEL_DEV, or use DEL_DEV_ASYNC. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.DelDev`; used by `Device.Close` (after STOP_DEV and queue teardown) and `ublk.DeleteDevice`.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_START_DEV
items.summary: Expose `/dev/ublkbN` once every queue has fetched all of its tags.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = the ublk server's pid (> 0). Since v6.17 (c2c8089f325e) it must equal the tgid
of the process that opened `/dev/ublkcN`; since v6.19-rc7 (47bdf1d29cae, 6.18.8) the comparison is done
in the init pid namespace so servers in a pid namespace work.

**Behaviour:** requires `UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_BASIC` from SET_PARAMS; builds `queue_limits` from the params;
waits interruptibly until every queue has every tag fetched (`ublk_wait_dev_ready_and_lock`, v7.2-rc5
432a9b2780c0; earlier `wait_for_completion_interruptible(&ub->completion)`); allocates the gendisk
`ublkbN`, applies capacity/read-only, sets state LIVE, `add_disk()`. Partition scanning is deferred to a
work item since v6.19 (7fc4da6a304b, backported 6.18.4) and skipped entirely for unprivileged daemons or
with `UBLK_F_NO_AUTO_PART_SCAN`.

**Errors:** `EINVAL` (pid <= 0, no BASIC params, pid mismatch), `EEXIST` (already LIVE or disk still in
use), `EINTR`, `EOPNOTSUPP` (zoned params without CONFIG_BLK_DEV_ZONED), `ENOMEM`, add_disk errors.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_START_DEV` (0x06, since v6.0).
items.notes: START_DEV blocks until the FETCHes arrive, so issue it from a thread other than the queue threads (or asynchronously). Before v6.5 (53e7d08f6d6e, backported 6.1.43) an interrupted wait was ignored. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.StartDev` with `os.Getpid()`; called by `Device.Start` after the queue engines have primed their FETCHes.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_STOP_DEV
items.summary: Remove `/dev/ublkbN` and abort the server's pending fetches.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `dev_id`; no buffer.

**Behaviour:** `ublk_stop_dev`: with a queueing recovery mode first force-aborts requeued requests
(`ublk_force_abort_dev`); `del_gendisk()` (waits for in-flight requests, so the server must keep serving
until STOP_DEV returns); state -> DEAD, `ublksrv_pid` -> -1; cancels the partition-scan work; then
completes every still-pending FETCH/COMMIT uring_cmd with `UBLK_IO_RES_ABORT` (`ublk_cancel_dev`).

**Result:** always 0 for an existing device (`ENODEV` otherwise).
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_STOP_DEV` (0x07, since v6.0).
items.notes: Not reversible in practice: ublksrv and go-ublk delete the device after stopping it. TRY_STOP_DEV is the variant that refuses while the disk is open. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_SET_PARAMS
items.summary: Set the device's `struct ublk_params` (block limits) before START_DEV.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `addr`/`len` -> `struct ublk_params`; the leading `len` field must be non-zero and <= header
`len`; `types` non-zero. The kernel copies `min(params.len, sizeof(kernel ublk_params))` bytes and masks
`types` with `UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_ALL` (unknown types silently dropped).

**Validation (`ublk_validate_params`):** BASIC mandatory: `9 <= logical_bs_shift <= PAGE_SHIFT` (lower
bound since v6.3-rc6 1d1665279a84), `physical_bs_shift`, `io_min_shift`, `io_opt_shift` <= 28 (v7.1-rc3
86f33ca9bea3), logical <= physical, `max_sectors <= max_io_buf_bytes >> 9`, `max_sectors >= PAGE_SIZE/512`
(v7.1-rc4 1860c2f85922; 6.12.92/6.18.34/7.0.11), zoned => `chunk_sectors` power of two (v7.3-rc1
2707acf1856d; 6.12.110/6.18.52/7.2.6). DISCARD: `max_discard_segments == 1` when `max_discard_sectors`,
`discard_granularity != 0`. DEVT is read-only (EINVAL). ZONED only with `UBLK_F_ZONED` and vice versa.
DMA_ALIGN, SEGMENT and INTEGRITY rules: see their entries. On any failure the stored params are zeroed.

**Errors:** `EINVAL`, `EACCES` (device already started: `UB_STATE_USED` since v6.14-rc6 5ac60242b017,
backported 6.1.131/6.6.83/6.12.19; before that only a LIVE device was refused, so SET_PARAMS during
recovery "succeeded" without effect), `EFAULT`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS` (0x08, since v6.0).
items.notes: Params are applied only by START_DEV. A newer server sending a longer `ublk_params` to an older kernel is fine (truncated); unknown types are dropped, so check GET_PARAMS if it matters. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.SetParams` / `SetDeviceParams` (BASIC, DISCARD, DMA_ALIGN, SEGMENT). ZONED and INTEGRITY are modeled in `uapi.UblkParams` but no public parameter sets them.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_GET_PARAMS
items.summary: Read back the device's `struct ublk_params`, with the read-only DEVT block filled in.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `addr`/`len`; the caller must store the buffer size in the leading `len` field

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_START_USER_RECOVERY
items.summary: Begin taking over a recoverable device whose previous server has exited.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `dev_id`; no buffer, no data.

**Preconditions (`ublk_ctrl_start_recovery`):** created with `UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY` (else `EINVAL`);
`/dev/ublkcN` no longer open (`UB_STATE_OPEN` clear — cleared at the end of the asynchronous release
work after the old server's fds and io_uring are gone) and state `QUIESCED` or `FAIL_IO` (else `EBUSY`).

**Version differences:** v6.1–v6.14: this command also reset every tag (`ublk_queue_reinit`), cleared
`ub->mm` (so the new process can mmap) and re-armed the readiness completion — it was mandatory.
v6.11-rc7 (e58f5142f883, 6.1.110/6.6.51) returns EINVAL instead of oopsing when no queue was ever ready.
Since v6.15 (728cbac5fe21) the reset happens in `ublk_ch_release_work_fn` and START_USER_RECOVERY is only
a precondition check; END_USER_RECOVERY no longer depends on it since v7.2-rc5 (432a9b2780c0).
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_START_USER_RECOVERY` (0x10, since v6.1).
items.notes: Poll: EBUSY is expected for a short while after the old server dies (release is asynchronous). The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.StartUserRecovery`; `ublk.Recover` retries EBUSY for up to 30 s.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_END_USER_RECOVERY
items.summary: Finish recovery: wait for the new server's fetches and put the device back to LIVE.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = new server pid (validated like START_DEV since v6.17).

**Behaviour (`ublk_ctrl_end_recovery`):** waits interruptibly until every queue has fetched every tag,
then requires a recoverable state (`EBUSY` otherwise) and `UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY` (`EINVAL`), stores the
pid, sets state LIVE and kicks the requeue list so requests held during the outage are dispatched to the
new server. v6.1–v6.14 unquiesced the block queue / cleared `fail_io` here instead.

**Errors:** `EINVAL` (pid mismatch, no recovery), `EBUSY`, `EINTR`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_END_USER_RECOVERY` (0x11, since v6.1).
items.notes: Before v7.2-rc5 the wait used a completion re-armed only by a successful START_USER_RECOVERY; skipping START could strand a requeued request (432a9b2780c0, backported 6.18.42/7.1.6). The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.EndUserRecovery`; `ublk.Recover` after the new queues have primed.

items.name: UBLK_CMD_END_USER_RECOVERY
items.details: Same handler as `UBLK_U_CMD_END_USER_RECOVERY`. The driver accepts a raw opcode (`_IOC_TYPE == 0`) only when built with `CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES=y` (`ublk_check_cmd_op`, v6.4+; check fixed in v6.4-rc2 e485bd9e2c41); without it the command fails with `EOPNOTSUPP`. On v6.0–v6.3 it is the only encoding. The number is also `_IOC_NR` of the ioctl form, which is what the driver switches on.
items.notes: Header: "Legacy command definition, don't use in new application". Ubuntu and the AL2023 6.18 kernel build with the legacy option off (see distro-kernels.md).

go_ublk.notes: go-ublk sends only the ioctl-encoded `UBLK_U_*` form (minimum kernel 6.8), so the raw opcode is never used. The number is modeled in `internal/uapi`.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO2
items.summary: GET_DEV_INFO that always carries the char-device path, so it works for unprivileged devices.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `addr` points at a buffer whose first `dev_path_len` bytes are the NUL-terminated path of
`/dev/ublkcN` (`dev_path_len` includes the NUL, <= PATH_MAX, <= `len`), followed by room for the 64-byte
info. The kernel checks the path names the device's char node (`ublk_char_dev_permission`: same rdev,
character device, `inode_permission(MAY_READ)`), then advances `addr`/`len` past the path.

**Privileged devices:** the caller still needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN *and* must supply the path (the only
command that requires a path on a privileged device).

**Errors:** as GET_DEV_INFO, plus `EINVAL` (missing/oversized path), `EPERM`/`ENOENT`/`EACCES` from the
path check.


Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO2` (0x12, since v6.3).
items.notes: ublk.rst recommends: try GET_DEV_INFO2 first, fall back to GET_DEV_INFO on kernels that lack it. The ioctl-encoded form exists since v6.4; on v6.0–v6.3 only the raw opcode works.

go_ublk.notes: ctrl.Controller.GetDevInfo2 (always sends the char-device path). The public GetDeviceInfo uses GET_DEV_INFO and adds the path automatically for unprivileged devices.

items.name: UBLK_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO2
items.details: Same handler as `UBLK_U_CMD_GET_DEV_INFO2`. The driver accepts a raw opcode (`_IOC_TYPE == 0`) only when built with `CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES=y` (`ublk_check_cmd_op`, v6.4+; check fixed in v6.4-rc2 e485bd9e2c41); without it the command fails with `EOPNOTSUPP`. On v6.0–v6.3 it is the only encoding. The number is also `_IOC_NR` of the ioctl form, which is what the driver switches on.
items.notes: Header: "Legacy command definition, don't use in new application". Ubuntu and the AL2023 6.18 kernel build with the legacy option off (see distro-kernels.md).

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_GET_FEATURES
items.details:
**Inputs:** `addr`/`len` with `len == UBLK_FEATURES_LEN` (8) exactly. `dev_id` is ignored: the command
is handled before any device lookup and before permission checks.

**Output:** the 64-bit `UBLK_F_ALL` of the running kernel (`UBLK_F_INTEGRITY` only when built with
CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INTEGRITY).

**Encoding gotcha:** `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd` compares the *full* opcode (`cmd_op ==
UBLK_U_CMD_GET_FEATURES`), unlike every other control command which is matched on `_IOC_NR`. An
`_IOWR`-encoded 0x13 therefore falls through to the device path and fails with `ENODEV` (or `EOPNOTSUPP`).

**Errors:** `EINVAL` (len != 8 or addr 0), `EFAULT`. Kernels before v6.5 do not know the command; with
`dev_id = -1` they fail it (`ENODEV` on v6.4).


No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_GET_FEATURES`).
items.notes: Any user who can open `/dev/ublk-control` may call it. kublk refuses to run without it (requires `UBLK_F_CMD_IOCTL_ENCODE`).

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.GetFeatures` (exact `_IOR` encoding); public `ublk.Probe`. Pre-6.5 kernels are treated as the v6.0 base set.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_DEL_DEV_ASYNC
items.summary: Remove a device without waiting for its id to be freed.
items.details:
Same as DEL_DEV (`ublk_ctrl_del_dev(wait=false)`): stop if needed, delete `/dev/ublkcN`, drop the
reference — but return immediately; the id becomes reusable when the last reference goes. Avoids the
close/munmap/unregister ordering problem of DEL_DEV.

**Broken dispatch in v6.9 and v6.10:** the switch compared `_IOC_NR(cmd_op)` with the full ioctl value,
so the command never matched and failed with `-ENOTSUPP` (524). Fixed in v6.11-rc1 (55fbb9a5d64e,
no stable backport). Usable from v6.11.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_DEL_DEV_ASYNC`).
items.notes: Header encodes it `_IOR` although it carries no output; the driver only checks `_IOC_NR`.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = new size in 512-byte sectors.

**Behaviour (`ublk_ctrl_set_size`):** stores it in `params.basic.dev_sectors` and calls
`set_capacity_and_notify()` (uevent with `RESIZE=1`; partitions are not rescanned). The driver does not
check `UBLK_F_UPDATE_SIZE`; the flag only advertises the command. No validation of the value.

**Errors:** `ENODEV` if the device has no disk (never started or stopped) — since v7.0-rc4
(25966fc09769, backported 6.18.20/6.19.9); v6.16–v6.19 kernels without it dereference NULL instead.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE`).
items.notes: The backend must already serve the new size when growing, and must stop accepting I/O beyond it only after shrinking.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.UpdateSize` (refuses a DEAD device to dodge the pre-7.0 NULL deref); public `Device.Resize`.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_QUIESCE_DEV
items.summary: Drain a LIVE device and abort the server's fetches so the server can hand over (live upgrade).
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = timeout in milliseconds (0 = wait forever; the value is passed to an
`unsigned int` parameter, so it is truncated to 32 bits).

**Behaviour (`ublk_ctrl_quiesce_dev`):** `EOPNOTSUPP` without `UBLK_F_QUIESCE`; `ENODEV` if no disk or
DEAD; returns 0 at once if not LIVE. Otherwise marks the device canceling (new requests are requeued),
waits until every queue has at least one idle tag whose FETCH can be cancelled (`ublk_wait_for_idle_io`;
skipped for BATCH_IO), then cancels all pending FETCH/COMMIT uring_cmds with `UBLK_IO_RES_ABORT`. The
server then exits/closes `/dev/ublkcN`; the release work moves the device to `QUIESCED` (or `FAIL_IO`),
ready for START/END_USER_RECOVERY by the next server.

**Errors:** `EOPNOTSUPP`, `ENODEV`, `EBUSY` (timeout: all I/O stayed with the server), `EINTR`.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_QUIESCE_DEV`).
items.notes: Requires UBLK_F_QUIESCE, which itself requires UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY at ADD_DEV.

go_ublk.notes: `ctrl.Controller.QuiesceDev`; used by `Device.Detach` when the device has QUIESCE (30 s timeout).

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_TRY_STOP_DEV
items.summary: STOP_DEV only if nobody has the block device open.
items.details:
**Behaviour (`ublk_ctrl_try_stop_dev`):** `ENODEV` if there is no disk; under `disk->open_mutex`,
`EBUSY` if `disk_openers() > 0`; otherwise sets `block_open` (further opens of `/dev/ublkbN` fail with
`ENXIO`) and performs STOP_DEV.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_TRY_STOP_DEV`).
items.notes: Advertised by `UBLK_F_SAFE_STOP_DEV`, which every v7.0+ kernel reports.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_REG_BUF
items.summary: Register a shared-memory buffer for UBLK_F_SHMEM_ZC zero copy; returns its index.
items.details:
**Inputs:** `addr` -> `struct ublk_shmem_buf_reg` (up to `len` bytes, max 24, copied; missing tail is
zero). `flags` may only be `UBLK_SHMEM_BUF_READ_ONLY`; `reserved` must be 0; `len` non-zero, page-aligned,
<= 4 GiB; `addr` page-aligned.

**Behaviour (`ublk_ctrl_reg_buf`):** long-term pins the pages (`FOLL_WRITE` unless READ_ONLY), freezes the
queue if started, allocates an index 0..65535 (IDA), inserts the PFN ranges into the device's maple tree.
Allowed before START_DEV (365ea7cc6244, same release).

**Result:** the buffer index (>= 0). **Errors:** `EOPNOTSUPP` (no SHMEM_ZC), `EINVAL`, `EFAULT` (partial
pin), `ENOMEM`, `ENOSPC` (indexes exhausted), `EEXIST` (pages already registered).
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_REG_BUF`).
items.notes: The registration struct is out of line precisely so an unprivileged caller can prefix the path at `addr`.

items.name: UBLK_U_CMD_UNREG_BUF
items.details:
**Inputs:** `data[0]` = index from REG_BUF. **Errors:** `EOPNOTSUPP` (no SHMEM_ZC), `EINVAL` (index >
65535), `ENOENT` (not registered). Unpins the pages after freezing the queue. All buffers are released
automatically when the device is freed.
Privileges: CAP_SYS_ADMIN for a privileged device; for a `UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV` device the caller must prefix the char-device path at `addr` and pass `dev_path_len` (see `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission`).

No raw/legacy opcode exists (the driver mirrors the number privately as `UBLK_CMD_UNREG_BUF`).

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_FETCH_REQ
items.summary: Arm a tag: hand the kernel one uring_cmd per (queue, tag) to complete when a request arrives.
items.details:
**SQE:** `struct ublksrv_io_cmd {q_id, tag, result (unused), addr}` in the SQE command area of
`/dev/ublkcN`'s io_uring. `addr` = server data buffer for this tag; required in copy mode unless
`UBLK_F_NEED_GET_DATA`; must be 0 with USER_COPY / SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY / AUTO_BUF_REG (`EINVAL`). With
`UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG`, `sqe->addr` carries a `ublk_auto_buf_reg` (buffer index + flags).

**Rules:** only before the device is ready (`EBUSY` once every queue has fetched all tags); once per tag
(`EINVAL` if already active); serialized by `ub->mutex`. The issuing task becomes the tag's daemon
(`io->task`); all later commands for the tag must come from it (per-queue daemon on v6.0–v6.15: the task
that issued the queue's last FETCH; per-I/O since v6.16). Not valid on a BATCH_IO device (`EOPNOTSUPP`).
On v6.0–v6.2 the I/O ring must use SQE128 too.

**CQE (when a request is dispatched to this tag):** `UBLK_IO_RES_OK` (descriptor at `io_cmd_buf[tag]` is
valid; for WRITE the data is already in `addr`), `UBLK_IO_RES_NEED_GET_DATA` (WRITE with NEED_GET_DATA),
`UBLK_IO_RES_ABORT` (device stopping / quiescing / server exiting: do not re-fetch), or a negative errno for
a rejected command.


Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_IO_FETCH_REQ` (0x20, since v6.0).
items.notes: Ioctl form since v6.4.

go_ublk.notes: `internal/queue` engine: one locked OS thread + io_uring per tag range primes every tag at start.

items.name: UBLK_IO_FETCH_REQ
items.details: Accepted only with `CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES=y` on v6.4+; the only form on v6.0–v6.3. The I/O path matches `_IOC_NR(cmd_op)`, so this number is also what the driver switches on.
items.notes: Header: "Legacy IO command definition, don't use in new application".

go_ublk.notes: go-ublk sends only the ioctl-encoded `UBLK_U_*` form (minimum kernel 6.8), so the raw opcode is never used. The number is modeled in `internal/uapi`.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ
items.summary: Complete the tag's current request with a result and re-arm the tag in one command.
items.details:
**SQE:** `ublksrv_io_cmd {q_id, tag, result, addr}`. `result` = bytes transferred (READ/WRITE) or 0, or a
negative errno; `addr` = buffer for the next request (copy mode; may be 0 with NEED_GET_DATA except for
READ) — for `UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_APPEND` it is instead `zone_append_lba` (the sector written). With
AUTO_BUF_REG, `sqe->addr` carries the next `ublk_auto_buf_reg`; the previous auto-registered buffer is
unregistered automatically if this SQE goes to the same io_uring.

**Rules:** must come from the tag's daemon task (`EINVAL` otherwise); the tag must be owned by the server
(`EBUSY` if a command is already pending); a stray COMMIT while NEED_GET_DATA is pending is `EINVAL`.

**Completion semantics:** see semantics.md §3 — negative results map through `errno_to_blk_status()`,
a 0-byte READ becomes `EIO`, short READ/WRITE results behave differently before and after v7.3-rc1.
The CQE for this SQE arrives with the *next* request (or ABORT).


Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_IO_COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ` (0x21, since v6.0).
items.notes: Ioctl form since v6.4.

go_ublk.notes: Engine commits with full length on success, negative errno on failure (`Request.Complete/CompleteN`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ
items.details: Accepted only with `CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES=y` on v6.4+; the only form on v6.0–v6.3. The I/O path matches `_IOC_NR(cmd_op)`, so this number is also what the driver switches on.
items.notes: Header: "Legacy IO command definition, don't use in new application".

go_ublk.notes: go-ublk sends only the ioctl-encoded `UBLK_U_*` form (minimum kernel 6.8), so the raw opcode is never used. The number is modeled in `internal/uapi`.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_NEED_GET_DATA
items.summary: Second step of a two-phase WRITE: supply the buffer and let the kernel copy the payload into it.
items.details:
Used only with `UBLK_F_NEED_GET_DATA` after a FETCH/COMMIT completed with `UBLK_IO_RES_NEED_GET_DATA`.
**SQE:** `{q_id, tag, addr = destination buffer}`. The kernel copies the WRITE data into `addr` and
completes *this* SQE with `UBLK_IO_RES_OK` (synchronously since v6.16; via task work before), after
which the descriptor is valid and the server handles the WRITE and later sends COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ.
Issuing it when not expected, or anything else when it is expected, is `EINVAL`. Must come from the
daemon task.


Legacy raw opcode: `UBLK_IO_NEED_GET_DATA` (0x22, since v6.0).
items.notes: Costs an extra round trip; only for servers that cannot pre-allocate per-tag buffers. Unavailable with USER_COPY/ZERO_COPY/AUTO_BUF_REG/BATCH_IO (flag cleared at ADD_DEV). Ioctl form since v6.4.

items.name: UBLK_IO_NEED_GET_DATA
items.details: Accepted only with `CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES=y` on v6.4+; the only form on v6.0–v6.3. The I/O path matches `_IOC_NR(cmd_op)`, so this number is also what the driver switches on.
items.notes: Header: "Legacy IO command definition, don't use in new application".

go_ublk.notes: go-ublk sends only the ioctl-encoded `UBLK_U_*` form (minimum kernel 6.8), so the raw opcode is never used. The number is modeled in `internal/uapi`.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_REGISTER_IO_BUF
items.summary: Zero copy: install an in-flight request's pages into the issuing io_uring's fixed-buffer table.
items.details:
**SQE:** `{q_id, tag, addr = buffer-table index}` sent on any io_uring that has a (sparse) registered
buffer table. The request's bvec becomes a kernel fixed buffer at that index
(`io_buffer_register_request`, named `io_buffer_register_bvec` before v7.3); the server then uses
`IORING_OP_READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED` or `IORING_URING_CMD_FIXED` against it. The ublk request cannot
complete until every registration is dropped (refcount, see `ublk_io` comments).

**Rules:** `UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY` required (`EINVAL`); request must be started and carry data.
On the daemon task it uses a cheap counter; off the daemon task it is allowed since v6.17
(`UBLK_F_BUF_REG_OFF_DAEMON`), on v6.15–v6.16 only the daemon may issue it. Also valid on BATCH_IO devices.


No raw opcode. On a BATCH_IO device the driver compares the full opcode value.
items.notes: Not available to unprivileged devices (kernel memory could leak if the server does not fill a READ).

go_ublk.notes: Zero-copy engine (`EnableZeroCopy`) when AUTO_BUF_REG is unavailable or falls back.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_UNREGISTER_IO_BUF
items.summary: Zero copy: remove a buffer installed by REGISTER_IO_BUF (or AUTO_BUF_REG).
items.details:
**SQE:** `{addr = buffer-table index}`; since v6.17 `q_id`/`tag` are ignored and any task may issue it
(`UBLK_F_BUF_REG_OFF_DAEMON`); on v6.15–v6.16 the q_id/tag of the registered request and the daemon task
were required. Calls `io_buffer_unregister()`; the request completes once its last registration is gone
and the server has committed it.


No raw opcode. On a BATCH_IO device the driver compares the full opcode value.

go_ublk.notes: Linked after the file I/O in the zero-copy engine.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_PREP_IO_CMDS
items.summary: BATCH_IO: arm many tags of one queue at once (batch FETCH_REQ).
items.details:
**SQE cmd area:** `struct ublk_batch_io {q_id, flags, nr_elem, elem_bytes}`; `sqe->addr` -> user buffer
of `nr_elem * elem_bytes` bytes of elements (`ublk_elem_header {tag, buf_index, result}` + optional
`__u64 buf_addr` if `UBLK_BATCH_F_HAS_BUF_ADDR` + optional `__u64 zone_lba` if `HAS_ZONE_LBA`).
`elem_bytes` must equal 8 + 8·HAS_BUF_ADDR + 8·HAS_ZONE_LBA; `nr_elem <= queue_depth` (`E2BIG`).
Flag rules (`ublk_check_batch_cmd`): HAS_ZONE_LBA needs ZONED; HAS_BUF_ADDR needs copy mode;
AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK needs AUTO_BUF_REG and excludes HAS_BUF_ADDR.

**Behaviour:** the buffer is snapshotted (v7.2-rc3 f01f5275feb7) and each tag is fetched as by FETCH_REQ
(no daemon task is recorded — any task may serve any tag). All-or-nothing: on an error the already
prepared tags are reverted. Returns 0 or a negative errno.


No raw opcode. On a BATCH_IO device the driver compares the full opcode value.
items.notes: Only on a device created with UBLK_F_BATCH_IO (its `/dev/ublkcN` uses `ublk_ch_batch_io_fops`).

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.BatchIO: one PREP_IO_CMDS per queue registers every tag.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_COMMIT_IO_CMDS
items.summary: BATCH_IO: commit results for many tags (and re-arm them).
items.details:
Same header and element format as PREP_IO_CMDS. Per element: `result` = completion result, `buf_addr` =
buffer for the next request (copy mode), `zone_lba` for zone append, `buf_index` for AUTO_BUF_REG.

**Result:** number of *bytes* of the element buffer processed (`iter.done`); elements after the first
failing one are not committed — divide by `elem_bytes` and retry the remainder. A negative errno only if
nothing was processed. Completions are batched through `blk_mq_end_request_batch()`.


No raw opcode. On a BATCH_IO device the driver compares the full opcode value.

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.BatchIO: each I/O thread commits a round's completions in one command, resubmitting unconsumed elements.

items.name: UBLK_U_IO_FETCH_IO_CMDS
items.summary: BATCH_IO: multishot fetch that delivers ready tags in provided buffers.
items.details:
**SQE:** must set `IORING_URING_CMD_MULTISHOT` (uring_cmd multishot exists since v6.18, 620a50c92700) and
use a provided-buffer ring (`sqe->buf_index` = buffer group); header `elem_bytes == 2`, `flags == 0`.

**CQEs:** each CQE consumes one provided buffer filled with `__u16` tags of requests now owned by the
server (res = byte count); read each tag's descriptor from the mmapped `io_cmd_buf`. Several FETCH_IO_CMDS
may be queued on a queue (load balancing across tasks) but only one is active at a time. The command
terminates with an error CQE (e.g. `-ENOBUFS` when no buffer can be selected, `UBLK_IO_RES_ABORT` on
cancel / quiesce, `-ENODEV` if the queue is canceling when attached).


No raw opcode. On a BATCH_IO device the driver compares the full opcode value.

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.BatchIO: multishot fetch into a 16 x 256-byte provided-buffer ring.

items.name: UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY
items.summary: Zero copy via io_uring kernel fixed buffers (REGISTER/UNREGISTER_IO_BUF).
items.details: Reserved in v6.0 but stripped by ADD_DEV (`flags &= ~UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY`, "We are not ready to support zero copy") on every kernel through v6.14. Functional since v6.15 (1f6540e2aabb): the kernel no longer copies data to/from the server buffer (`ublk_need_map_io()` false), FETCH/COMMIT must pass `addr = 0`, and the server reaches request pages only through REGISTER_IO_BUF + fixed-buffer io_uring ops. Decoupled from USER_COPY in v6.15-rc5 (69edf98be844). The server should align `ublk_param_dma_align` and `ublk_param_segment` with its backend. Clears NEED_GET_DATA.
items.notes: On 6.0–6.14 the bit is silently dropped from the negotiated flags, so check the written-back flags.

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.EnableZeroCopy` with a `ZeroCopyBackend` (a backing file): the engine registers each request buffer (AUTO_BUF_REG when the kernel lists it, otherwise REGISTER_IO_BUF + linked UNREGISTER_IO_BUF) and reads/writes the file with fixed-buffer ops, fdatasync and fallocate on the queue's ring. Not offered to Handlers; excludes user copy, NEED_GET_DATA and unprivileged.

items.name: UBLK_F_URING_CMD_COMP_IN_TASK
items.summary: Always dispatch requests to the server via io_uring_cmd_complete_in_task().
items.details: v6.0–v6.4: selected `io_uring_cmd_complete_in_task()` instead of `task_work_add()` for dispatch (task_work_add was only usable when ublk_drv was built in; for a module the flag was forced on since v6.1-rc4, 224e858f215a). v6.5 removed the task_work_add path (29dc5d06613f) and forces the flag on in every ADD_DEV reply; it has no effect since.
items.notes: Informational only on v6.5+.

go_ublk.notes: Not requested; the kernel forces it on and ignores it since 6.5.

items.name: UBLK_F_NEED_GET_DATA
items.summary: Two-phase WRITE: deliver WRITEs without data, server supplies the buffer with UBLK_U_IO_NEED_GET_DATA.
items.details: For WRITE requests (v6.0–v6.3 also FLUSH) the FETCH/COMMIT CQE returns `UBLK_IO_RES_NEED_GET_DATA`; the server allocates a buffer and issues NEED_GET_DATA, the kernel copies the payload and completes it with `UBLK_IO_RES_OK`. FETCH may pass `addr = 0`; COMMIT may pass `addr = 0` unless the request is a READ. Cleared by ADD_DEV when combined with USER_COPY (v6.5+), SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY or AUTO_BUF_REG (v6.15/6.16+) or BATCH_IO (v7.0+).
items.notes: Added for servers with existing buffer management; costs an extra round trip per WRITE.

items.name: UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY
items.summary: Keep the device (and /dev/ublkbN) when the server dies so a new server can recover it.
items.details: When the server exits, `ublk_ch_release_work_fn` aborts what the server held and moves the device to `UBLK_S_DEV_QUIESCED` (or `FAIL_IO` with RECOVERY_FAIL_IO) instead of stopping it. Requests issued to the server are failed with EIO (default), requeued (REISSUE) or failed (FAIL_IO); new requests are requeued (default/REISSUE) or failed with `BLK_STS_TARGET` (FAIL_IO). A new server recovers with START_USER_RECOVERY, re-opens/mmaps `/dev/ublkcN`, fetches every tag, then END_USER_RECOVERY. Silently cleared for unprivileged devices. Full protocol and version history: semantics.md §9.
items.notes: Recovery was reworked in v6.15 (detection moved to char-device release; reset moved out of START_USER_RECOVERY). Known unfixed-before-v7.1 UAF on the recovery reset path: f7700a4415af.

items.name: UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY_REISSUE
items.summary: With USER_RECOVERY: requeue (re-issue) requests that were with the dead server.
items.details: `__ublk_fail_req` requeues instead of failing outstanding requests (`ublk_nosrv_should_reissue_outstanding`), so the new server sees them again after END_USER_RECOVERY. The backend must tolerate a write being applied twice. Silently cleared for unprivileged devices. Only valid together with USER_RECOVERY and not with FAIL_IO (EINVAL since v6.13, d00c0ea17955).

items.name: UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV
items.summary: Let a non-root user create and own a device.
items.details: ADD_DEV without CAP_SYS_ADMIN requires this flag (else EPERM); with CAP_SYS_ADMIN the flag is cleared. The kernel records the caller's uid/gid; every later control command must carry the `/dev/ublkcN` path prefix (`dev_path_len`) and pass an inode permission check; only the owner may open `/dev/ublkbN` (v6.3, 48a905198024); partitions are never scanned; an I/O timeout SIGKILLs the server (v6.4, c0b79b0ff53b); at most `ublks_max` (default 64) such devices exist. USER_RECOVERY/REISSUE are silently dropped; USER_COPY (v6.12, 42aafd8b48ad, 6.6.58), SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY (v6.15) and AUTO_BUF_REG (v6.16) are rejected. Needs a udev rule making `/dev/ublk-control` accessible and chowning `ublkc*`/`ublkb*` to owner_uid/gid.
items.notes: Before v6.12 an unprivileged USER_COPY server could leak uninitialized kernel memory by under-filling READs.

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.EnableUnprivileged`; every control command gets the path prefix automatically (`ctrl.devRequest`).

items.name: UBLK_F_CMD_IOCTL_ENCODE
items.summary: Advertises that the kernel accepts ioctl-encoded (`UBLK_U_*`) opcodes.
items.details: Set in every ADD_DEV reply since v6.4 (`flags |= UBLK_F_CMD_IOCTL_ENCODE`); the driver never reads the bit from the request. Its presence in GET_FEATURES / the ADD_DEV reply is how a server knows `UBLK_U_*` opcodes work.

go_ublk.notes: Always requested; go-ublk sends only ioctl-encoded opcodes.

items.name: UBLK_F_USER_COPY
items.summary: Move data with pread()/pwrite() on /dev/ublkcN instead of kernel copies into a server buffer.
items.details: The kernel never touches the server buffer; FETCH/COMMIT pass `addr = 0` (except ZONE_APPEND's LBA). The server copies with `pread`/`pwrite` (or io_uring READ/WRITE) at offset `UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET + (q_id << UBLK_QID_OFF) + (tag << UBLK_TAG_OFF) + byte_offset` (+ `UBLKSRV_IO_INTEGRITY_FLAG` for the integrity buffer): read() copies a WRITE/ZONE_APPEND payload out, write() fills a READ/REPORT_ZONES. Allowed only while the server owns the request. Required by ZONED (or ZERO_COPY) and INTEGRITY. Rejected for unprivileged devices since v6.12. Details: semantics.md §5.
items.notes: Per-request data is limited to 32 MiB by the 25-bit offset field.

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.EnableUserCopy`; the engine pread/pwrites on the char fd.

items.name: UBLK_F_ZONED
items.details: Requires CONFIG_BLK_DEV_ZONED and USER_COPY or SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY (ADD_DEV EINVAL otherwise) and `UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_ZONED` params (with `chunk_sectors` = zone size, a power of two). Adds the zone operations, `UBLK_IO_OP_REPORT_ZONES` (server fills a `struct blk_zone` array), and zone append, whose written sector is returned in COMMIT's `zone_append_lba`.
items.notes: UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY also satisfies the requirement (v6.15+).

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.EnableZoned` + `Zoned` (zone size, open/active limits, max append); Handler-only (zone ops, `Request.ReportZones`, `CompleteZoneAppend`); user copy is turned on automatically.

items.name: UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY_FAIL_IO
items.summary: With USER_RECOVERY: fail all I/O while no server is attached, instead of queueing it.
items.details: After the server dies the device goes to `UBLK_S_DEV_FAIL_IO`: outstanding requests fail with EIO, new requests fail immediately with `BLK_STS_TARGET` (`ublk_prep_req`), until a new server completes recovery. Valid only with USER_RECOVERY and not with REISSUE.

items.name: UBLK_F_UPDATE_SIZE
items.details: Purely informational: the driver does not check the bit when handling UPDATE_SIZE.

go_ublk.notes: Requested when the kernel lists it; `Device.Resize`.

items.name: UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG
items.summary: Zero copy without explicit commands: register each request buffer automatically before dispatch.
items.details: FETCH/COMMIT pass a `ublk_auto_buf_reg` in `sqe->addr` (index + flags, reserved fields 0, else EINVAL). Before completing the fetch CQE the kernel registers the request bvec at that index in the *same* io_uring's sparse buffer table and unregisters it at COMMIT (if COMMIT goes to the same ring; otherwise the server must UNREGISTER_IO_BUF). If registration fails: with `UBLK_AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK` the CQE is delivered with `UBLK_IO_F_NEED_REG_BUF` set in the descriptor; without it the request is failed with EIO and the uring_cmd stays pending. Compatible with SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY; clears NEED_GET_DATA; rejected for unprivileged devices.
items.notes: Buffer table max 16K entries per io_uring.

go_ublk.notes: Requested automatically with `EnableZeroCopy` when the kernel lists it; FETCH/COMMIT carry `{Index: tag, Flags: UBLK_AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK}` and a request arriving with `UBLK_IO_F_NEED_REG_BUF` is registered manually.

items.name: UBLK_F_QUIESCE
items.summary: Enables UBLK_U_CMD_QUIESCE_DEV (drain for live server upgrade).
items.details: Must be combined with USER_RECOVERY (ADD_DEV EINVAL otherwise). QUIESCE_DEV returns EOPNOTSUPP without it.

go_ublk.notes: Requested with any RecoveryMode when the kernel lists it; used by `Device.Detach`.

items.name: UBLK_F_PER_IO_DAEMON
items.summary: Each (queue, tag) may have its own daemon task instead of one task per queue.
items.details: Capability flag: v6.16+ always report it (except with BATCH_IO, where the kernel clears it since there is no daemon at all). The task that issues a tag's FETCH_REQ owns that tag; other tags of the same queue can be served by other tasks, so a server can spread one hot queue over several threads. On older kernels all tags of a queue must be served by one task.

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.ThreadsPerQueue > 1` splits a queue's tags across engines (requires the flag).

items.name: UBLK_F_BUF_REG_OFF_DAEMON
items.summary: REGISTER/UNREGISTER_IO_BUF may be issued from any task.
items.details: Capability flag always reported since v6.17. UNREGISTER_IO_BUF also ignores q_id/tag.

go_ublk.notes: go-ublk issues REGISTER/UNREGISTER_IO_BUF on the tag's own engine thread, so it never needs off-daemon registration.

items.name: UBLK_F_BATCH_IO
items.summary: Per-queue batch I/O commands (PREP/COMMIT/FETCH_IO_CMDS) replace per-tag FETCH/COMMIT.
items.details: The device's char node uses `ublk_ch_batch_io_fops`; per-tag FETCH_REQ/COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ/NEED_GET_DATA are rejected; REGISTER/UNREGISTER_IO_BUF still work. No daemon task: any task can serve any tag. Clears PER_IO_DAEMON and NEED_GET_DATA. FETCH_IO_CMDS needs multishot uring_cmd (v6.18+ io_uring) and provided buffer rings. Protocol: semantics.md §8.
items.notes: Several recovery fixes landed after 7.0 (e4c4bfec2bb8, 8a14be55bdc6 [7.2.7]).

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.BatchIO (copy and user-copy modes; not with zero copy).

items.name: UBLK_F_INTEGRITY
items.summary: Requests may carry an integrity/metadata (PI) buffer.
items.details: Requires USER_COPY (ADD_DEV EINVAL) and a kernel with CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INTEGRITY (otherwise absent from UBLK_F_ALL). Configure with `UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_INTEGRITY`; requests with metadata have `UBLK_IO_F_INTEGRITY` set and the server reads/writes the metadata with pread/pwrite at the user-copy offset OR'ed with `UBLKSRV_IO_INTEGRITY_FLAG` (bit 62).

go_ublk.notes: `DeviceParams.Integrity` (`IntegrityParams`: metadata size, interval, checksum, reftag, PI offset, tag size); user copy forced on; Backends implement `IntegrityBackend`, Handlers get `Request.Integrity`.

items.name: UBLK_F_SAFE_STOP_DEV
items.details: Always reported since v7.0.

items.name: UBLK_F_NO_AUTO_PART_SCAN
items.summary: Do not scan partitions when the device starts.
items.details: START_DEV skips the async partition scan and clears `GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN` (only for trusted daemons; v7.0-rc4 155a3bedccaf) so a later `BLKRRPART` works.

items.name: UBLK_F_SHMEM_ZC
items.summary: Shared-memory zero copy: requests whose pages lie in a registered buffer arrive by reference.
items.details: The server registers memfd/hugetlbfs memory it shares with clients via UBLK_U_CMD_REG_BUF. When a request's pages all fall contiguously inside one registered buffer (PFN maple-tree match, `ublk_try_buf_match`) the descriptor gets `UBLK_IO_F_SHMEM_ZC` and `addr = ublk_shmem_zc_addr(index, offset)`; no copy happens in either direction. Non-matching requests use the normal path. A READ_ONLY buffer only matches WRITEs. Only O_DIRECT client I/O can match.

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.SharedMemoryZeroCopy; requests in registered regions arrive with FlagSharedMemory and Data pointing into the region.

items.name: UBLK_F_IO_DESC_SIZE
items.summary: Server chooses the per-tag descriptor stride (`ublksrv_ctrl_dev_info.io_desc_size`).
items.details: With the flag, ADD_DEV takes `io_desc_size` (24..256, multiple of 8) from dev_info (former `pad0`); otherwise it is set to 24. The mmapped descriptor array uses that stride: descriptor of tag *t* at `t * io_desc_size`, mmap length `round_up(depth * io_desc_size, PAGE_SIZE)`, and queue *q* at offset `q * round_up(4096 * io_desc_size, PAGE_SIZE)`. Bytes past the 24-byte `ublksrv_io_desc` are reserved for future kernel fields.
items.notes: Unreleased as of 2026-10-04 (v7.3-rc).

go_ublk.notes: DeviceParams.IODescSize; the engine honors the stride and exposes the extra bytes as Request.DescriptorExtra.

items.name: UBLK_S_DEV_DEAD
items.summary: No block device: just added, or stopped.
items.details: Set at ADD_DEV (forced since e65848e4ce35) and by `ublk_detach_disk` on STOP_DEV / DEL_DEV / server exit without recovery. SET_PARAMS works only before the first START_DEV.

items.name: UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE
items.details: Entered by START_DEV (before `add_disk`) and END_USER_RECOVERY.

items.name: UBLK_S_DEV_QUIESCED
items.summary: Server gone (or QUIESCE_DEV), requests held for a recovering server.
items.details: Recovery mode without FAIL_IO. Since v6.15 the block queue is *not* quiesced; requests are requeued via the canceling flag until END_USER_RECOVERY kicks the requeue list (v6.1–v6.14: `blk_mq_quiesce_queue`).

items.name: UBLK_S_DEV_FAIL_IO
items.summary: Server gone, all I/O failing until a server recovers the device.
items.details: Only with UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY_FAIL_IO. New requests get `BLK_STS_TARGET` (-EREMOTEIO in userspace).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_READ
items.details: Result: bytes read (>0). A 0 result is turned into EIO. Copy mode: the kernel copies `result` bytes from the server buffer; a short result completes that many bytes and requeues the rest (all versions). With USER_COPY/zero copy a short positive result completed only that part before v7.3-rc1 but completes the *whole* request since a8a79eba22dc.

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE
items.details: Result: bytes written. v6.0–v7.2: a short result completes that many bytes and requeues the remainder (a 0 result requeues the whole request); v7.3-rc1+ (a8a79eba22dc): any non-negative result completes the entire request — return the full length or an errno.

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH
items.details: Sent only if the device advertises `UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE`. No data, `nr_sectors` 0. Result 0 or errno. Preflush/FUA on writes are turned into separate FLUSH requests by the block layer unless `UBLK_ATTR_FUA` is also set.

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_DISCARD
items.details: Sent only if DISCARD params set `max_discard_sectors`. No data; may exceed `max_io_buf_bytes` (range ops are not bounded by the data buffer). Single segment only.

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE_SAME
items.details: `ublk_setup_iod` has no mapping for it (REQ_OP_WRITE_SAME left the block layer in 5.18), so no kernel ever sends it.

go_ublk.notes: Constant only; never sent by the kernel.

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE_ZEROES
items.details: Sent only if `max_write_zeroes_sectors` is set. No data. `UBLK_IO_F_NOUNMAP` means the range must stay allocated.

items.details: Zoned devices only.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_CLOSE
items.details: Zoned devices only.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_FINISH
items.details: Zoned devices only.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_APPEND
items.summary: Append data to a zone; the server picks the sector.
items.details: Data flows like WRITE (USER_COPY read()/zero copy). Return the sector actually written in COMMIT's `zone_append_lba` (`req->__sector = addr`); in batch mode in the element's `zone_lba` with `UBLK_BATCH_F_HAS_ZONE_LBA`.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_RESET_ALL
items.details: Zoned devices only.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_ZONE_RESET
items.details: Zoned devices only.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_OP_REPORT_ZONES
items.details: Carried as REQ_OP_DRV_IN: `start_sector` = first zone, `nr_zones` (union with nr_sectors) = max zones. The server fills a `struct blk_zone` array (linux/blkzoned.h) into the request buffer (write() in USER_COPY mode); a zero-length entry ends the report early. Result = bytes.

go_ublk.notes: Delivered to a Handler on a zoned device (`EnableZoned`, `ublk.Op*`).

items.name: UBLK_IO_F_FAILFAST_DEV
items.summary: REQ_FAILFAST_DEV: don't retry on device errors.
items.details: Set from `req->cmd_flags` by `ublk_req_build_flags`. Advisory; a server may ignore it.

go_ublk.notes: Passed to Handlers on Request.Flags (ublk.Flag*); a hint a Backend may ignore.

items.name: UBLK_IO_F_FAILFAST_TRANSPORT
items.summary: REQ_FAILFAST_TRANSPORT: don't retry on transport errors.
items.details: Set from `req->cmd_flags` by `ublk_req_build_flags`. Advisory; a server may ignore it.

go_ublk.notes: Passed to Handlers on Request.Flags (ublk.Flag*); a hint a Backend may ignore.

items.name: UBLK_IO_F_FAILFAST_DRIVER
items.summary: REQ_FAILFAST_DRIVER: don't retry on driver errors.
items.details: Set from `req->cmd_flags` by `ublk_req_build_flags`. Advisory; a server may ignore it.

items.name: UBLK_IO_F_META
items.details: Set from `req->cmd_flags` by `ublk_req_build_flags`. Advisory; a server may ignore it.

go_ublk.notes: Passed to Handlers on Request.Flags (ublk.Flag*); a hint a Backend may ignore.

items.name: UBLK_IO_F_FUA
items.summary: REQ_FUA: the write must be durable before completion.
items.details: Only appears if the device advertises `UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE | UBLK_ATTR_FUA`; otherwise the block layer emulates FUA with a post-flush and the bit is never set. A server that advertises FUA must make such writes durable before completing them.

items.details: Set from `req->cmd_flags` by `ublk_req_build_flags`. Advisory; a server may ignore it.

items.details: Set only when the server passed `UBLK_AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK` (or `UBLK_BATCH_F_AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK`) and `io_buffer_register_request` failed; the CQE is delivered anyway and the server must register the buffer itself or use user copy.

items.name: struct ublksrv_io_desc
items.summary: Per-tag request descriptor in the read-only mmapped command buffer of `/dev/ublkcN`.
items.details: Queue *q*'s array is mapped at offset `q * round_up(UBLK_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH * io_desc_size, PAGE_SIZE)` with length exactly `round_up(queue_depth * io_desc_size, PAGE_SIZE)` (`ublk_ch_mmap`; `EINVAL` otherwise, `EPERM` for a writable mapping, and since v7.3-rc2 VM_MAYWRITE is cleared so mprotect cannot make it writable). Before v6.13 (d369735e02ef, 6.1.120/6.6.64/6.12.2) the queue stride was not page-rounded, which broke multi-queue on 64K-page kernels. Valid to read after the tag's CQE returns OK; written by the kernel on the daemon task (v7.3).

items.name: ublksrv_io_desc.nr_sectors
items.summary: Length in 512-byte sectors (union `nr_zones` for REPORT_ZONES since v6.6).

items.name: ublksrv_io_desc.addr
items.summary: Server buffer address for this request (copy mode), or the SHMEM_ZC encoding.

items.name: struct ublksrv_io_cmd
items.details: Fits a normal 64-byte SQE command area (SQE128 not required since v6.3).

items.name: ublksrv_io_cmd.result
items.summary: COMMIT only: bytes or negative errno.

items.name: ublksrv_io_cmd.addr
items.summary: Buffer address (copy mode), buffer-table index (REGISTER/UNREGISTER), or zone_append_lba (union since v6.6).

items.name: struct ublk_auto_buf_reg
items.summary: AUTO_BUF_REG registration request, packed into `sqe->addr` of FETCH/COMMIT.
items.details: Packing: bits 0-15 index, 16-23 flags, 24-31 reserved0, 32-63 reserved1 (`ublk_auto_buf_reg_to_sqe_addr`). Reserved fields must be zero and flags within `UBLK_AUTO_BUF_REG_F_MASK` (`EINVAL`, validated before the uring_cmd is taken since v7.3-rc1 ca5a01eee34c).

items.name: ublk_auto_buf_reg.index
items.summary: Buffer-table slot for the request buffer.

items.name: struct ublk_elem_header
items.summary: Mandatory 8-byte head of each BATCH_IO element.
items.details: Element = header [+ `__u64 buf_addr` if HAS_BUF_ADDR] [+ `__u64 zone_lba` if HAS_ZONE_LBA].

go_ublk.notes: Modeled only. Used by batch I/O.

items.name: struct ublk_batch_io
items.summary: BATCH_IO command header in the SQE command area; elements live at `sqe->addr`.
items.details: `nr_elem * elem_bytes` bytes of elements; see UBLK_U_IO_PREP_IO_CMDS.

go_ublk.notes: Modeled only. Used by batch I/O.

items.name: struct ublk_param_basic
items.details: All sector counts are 512-byte sectors regardless of logical block size.

items.name: ublk_param_basic.max_sectors
items.summary: Max request size in sectors; <= max_io_buf_bytes>>9 and >= PAGE_SIZE>>9 (v7.1+).

items.name: ublk_param_basic.chunk_sectors
items.summary: Chunk / zone size in sectors (power of two when zoned).

items.name: struct ublk_param_discard
items.details: Validated: `max_discard_segments == 1` when max_discard_sectors != 0; `discard_granularity != 0`.

items.name: struct ublk_param_devt
items.summary: UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_DEVT: device numbers, filled by GET_PARAMS (setting it is EINVAL).

items.name: struct ublk_param_zoned
items.details: Validated (`ublk_dev_param_zoned_validate`): device must be ZONED; `max_zone_append_sectors != 0`; open/active <= nr_zones (= dev_sectors / chunk_sectors).

items.name: ublk_param_zoned.max_zone_append_sectors
items.summary: Max zone-append size; must be non-zero.

items.name: struct ublk_param_dma_align
items.details: `alignment` is a mask: alignment+1 must be a power of two and alignment < PAGE_SIZE. Default without it: 3 (since v6.10, 928b607d1a09).

items.name: ublk_param_dma_align.alignment
items.summary: DMA alignment mask (e.g. 4095 for page alignment).

items.name: struct ublk_param_segment
items.details: seg_boundary_mask+1 power of two and >= 4096; max_segment_size >= 4096; a zero max_segments is undefined (header comment). Defaults without it: USHRT_MAX segments of UINT_MAX bytes (since v6.9-rc7, eaf4a9b19b99).

items.name: struct ublk_param_integrity
items.details: Validated: UBLK_F_INTEGRITY set; flags only LBMD_PI_CAP_INTEGRITY|LBMD_PI_CAP_REFTAG; csum_type one of LBMD_PI_CSUM_NONE/IP/CRC16_T10DIF/CRC64_NVME (tuple 0/8/8/16 bytes); metadata_size != 0; REFTAG needs a checksum; pi_offset + tuple <= metadata_size; 9 <= interval_exp <= logical_bs_shift. Applied as `queue_limits.integrity` at START_DEV.

items.name: ublk_param_integrity.pi_offset
items.summary: Offset of the PI tuple in the metadata.

items.name: struct ublk_params
items.summary: SET_PARAMS/GET_PARAMS container: `len`, `types`, then every parameter block at a fixed offset.
items.details: sizeof by version (8-byte aligned): 64 (v6.0–v6.2: basic, discard), 80 (v6.3: +devt), 112 (v6.6: +zoned), 136 (v6.15: +dma, seg; seg is 8-byte aligned so 4 bytes of padding precede it), 152 (v7.0: +integrity). The kernel copies `min(len, sizeof)` both ways, so mismatched userspace/kernel sizes interoperate.

items.name: ublk_params.len
items.summary: Byte length of the struct as sent/received; set by the caller for both SET and GET.

items.name: struct ublk_shmem_buf_reg
items.details: `len` was widened from __u32 to __u64 within the v7.1 merge window (23b3b6f0b584), so every release has the 24-byte form.

go_ublk.notes: Modeled; used by the internal RegBuf. Used by shared-memory zero copy.

items.name: ublk_shmem_buf_reg.addr
items.summary: Page-aligned VA of the shared mapping.

items.name: UBLK_IO_RES_OK
items.summary: Fetch CQE result: a request is ready in the descriptor.

items.name: UBLK_IO_RES_NEED_GET_DATA
items.summary: Fetch CQE result: WRITE needs UBLK_U_IO_NEED_GET_DATA first.

items.name: UBLK_IO_RES_ABORT
items.summary: Fetch CQE result: tag cancelled (stop, quiesce, exit); do not re-fetch.
items.notes: The header: "only ABORT means that no re-fetch". Since v7.1-rc3 (845db023a8ae) a command issued from fallback task work can also complete with -ECANCELED.

items.name: UBLKSRV_CMD_BUF_OFFSET
items.summary: mmap offset of queue 0's descriptor array.

items.name: UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET
items.summary: Base file offset for USER_COPY pread/pwrite.
items.notes: Defined in v6.0 but unused until USER_COPY (v6.5).

items.name: UBLK_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH
items.summary: Max tags per queue; also fixes the descriptor mmap stride.

items.name: UBLK_IO_BUF_OFF
items.summary: Bit offset of the byte offset in a user-copy position.

items.name: UBLK_IO_BUF_BITS
items.summary: Byte-offset width: 32 MiB per request in user copy.

items.name: UBLK_TAG_OFF
items.summary: Bit offset of the tag in a user-copy position.

items.name: UBLK_QID_OFF
items.summary: Bit offset of the queue id in a user-copy position.

items.name: UBLK_MAX_NR_QUEUES
items.summary: Max hardware queues (ADD_DEV enforces it since v6.16).

items.name: UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_TOTAL_SIZE
items.summary: Size of the user-copy position space.

items.name: UBLK_INTEGRITY_FLAG_OFF
items.summary: Bit selecting the integrity buffer in a user-copy position.

go_ublk.notes: Used by the integrity user-copy path.

items.name: UBLKSRV_IO_INTEGRITY_FLAG
items.summary: OR into the pread/pwrite offset to copy the integrity buffer.
items.notes: EINVAL without UBLK_F_INTEGRITY.

items.name: UBLK_SHMEM_BUF_READ_ONLY
items.summary: REG_BUF flag: pin without FOLL_WRITE (works with write-sealed memfds); buffer matches only WRITEs.

go_ublk.notes: Modeled. Used by shared-memory zero copy.

items.name: UBLK_AUTO_BUF_REG_FALLBACK
items.summary: auto_buf_reg flag: on registration failure deliver the request with UBLK_IO_F_NEED_REG_BUF instead of failing it.

go_ublk.notes: Always set by the zero-copy engine.
Always set by the zero-copy engine.

items.name: UBLK_BATCH_F_HAS_ZONE_LBA
items.summary: Batch elements carry a __u64 zone_lba (needs ZONED).

go_ublk.notes: Set for batch I/O on zoned devices.

items.name: UBLK_BATCH_F_HAS_BUF_ADDR
items.summary: Batch elements carry a __u64 buf_addr (copy mode only).

go_ublk.notes: Set for batch I/O in copy mode.
Set for batch I/O with zero copy: elements carry buf_index = tag, with the NEED_REG_BUF fallback handled by a manual REGISTER_IO_BUF.
Modeled. Used by shared-memory zero copy.

items.name: UBLK_SHMEM_ZC_IDX_MASK
items.summary: SHMEM_ZC addr bits 32-47: buffer index (48-63 reserved).

go_ublk.notes: Modeled. Used by shared-memory zero copy.

items.name: CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK
items.summary: Kconfig: builds ublk_drv ("Userspace block driver (Experimental)", selects IO_URING).
items.notes: Not a header element. Module name ublk_drv; no devname alias, so `modprobe ublk_drv` is needed before /dev/ublk-control exists. Distro status: distro-kernels.md.

go_ublk.notes: Runtime requirement; `Probe` explains a missing module.

items.name: CONFIG_BLKDEV_UBLK_LEGACY_OPCODES
items.summary: Kconfig: keep accepting the raw (pre-6.4) opcodes.
items.notes: Not a header element. With =n, `ublk_check_cmd_op` rejects any opcode whose `_IOC_TYPE` is not 'u' with EOPNOTSUPP. Ubuntu (all kernels) and AL2023 kernel6.18 build it =n.

go_ublk.notes: Irrelevant: go-ublk only sends ioctl-encoded opcodes.

items.name: ublks_max (module parameter)
items.summary: Module parameter limiting how many devices may be added.
items.notes: Not a header element. v6.3–v6.6: read-only (0444), limits *all* devices; v6.7 (6eba24aeb5e2): writable at runtime, 0..2^20; v6.15 (80bdfbb3545b): limits only UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV devices (internally `unprivileged_ublks_max`). Exceeding it: ADD_DEV EACCES. Device ids are allocated lowest-free from 0 up to 2^20-1 (bounded since v6.7, 56974c07f2c7).

go_ublk.notes: ListDevices enumerates /sys/class/ublk-char, so device IDs beyond 63 are found; the 0..63 probe is only a fallback without sysfs.

items.name: UBLK_MAX_UBLKS (driver)
items.summary: Driver-internal: device ids must be < 2^20 (char minor space).
items.notes: Not in the UAPI header.

items.name: UBLK_MAX_IO_DESC_SIZE (driver)
items.summary: Driver-internal: largest io_desc_size accepted with UBLK_F_IO_DESC_SIZE.
items.notes: Not in the UAPI header.

items.name: UBLK_SHMEM_BUF_SIZE_MAX (driver)
items.notes: Not in the UAPI header.

go_ublk.notes: Documented on RegBuf. Used by shared-memory zero copy.
